$description: GENERIC, SWAPPABLE chart-palette TEMPLATE (decision B2). Ships the dataviz skill's validated default so charts are color-blind-safe out of the box. A tenant substitutes the categorical slots to match their brand and MUST re-run scripts/validate_palette.mjs (light AND dark) before shipping — the CI gate enforces this. Status is fixed and never themed. Chart chrome + categorical dark steps also drive dist/tokens.css chart-* vars.

meta.swap_procedure: 1) replace categorical.light/.dark slots with brand hues; 2) node scripts/validate_palette.mjs "<light csv>" --mode light; 3) --mode dark --surface <dark chart surface>; 4) fix any FAIL via snap-to-passing (hold hue, nudge lightness one step, re-run); 5) sub-3:1 contrast slots are legal ONLY if the chart ships direct labels or the table-view twin.

light.note: slots 3,4,5 sit sub-3:1 on the light surface -> relief rule (labels/table required).

validated.all_pairs_cap: Only the first 3 slots clear the all-pairs floors; scatter/bubble/choropleth/small-multiples cap at 3 series -> fold tail to 'Other' or facet.

categorical.$description: 8 fixed-order hues. Assign slots in sequence; NEVER cycle past 8 (fold to 'Other'/facet). Order is the CVD-safety mechanism — do not reorder without re-validating.

sequential.$description: One hue (blue), magnitude light->dark. Heatmaps/choropleths. Ordinal marks (funnel/tiers) must keep the surface-nearest step >=2:1 (light: no lighter than step 250; dark: no darker than step 600). Validate ramps with --ordinal, NOT the categorical checks.

diverging.$description: Blue <-> red poles (warm/cool = opposite), equal steps per arm, gray midpoint that reads as 'nothing'.

status.$description: FIXED — never themed, deliberately distinct from categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series. ALWAYS render with an icon + label (color never carries meaning alone). On the light surface warning+serious are sub-3:1 BY DESIGN — the icon+label pairing is the mitigation. Names map: good=success, warning=warn, critical=error.

chrome.$description: Chart-frame ink/lines. Same token NAMES in light+dark; values differ. Text never wears a data color — labels/axes/values use these ink tokens.
